summary.text: Random number generation produces a sequence of numbers or symbols that cannot reasonably be predicted better than by random chance.
True random generators draw on a physical environment that keeps changing in ways practically impossible to model, while pseudorandom generators are predetermined.
A pseudorandom generator can be rerun from the same starting state, which makes debugging Monte Carlo simulations easier.

facts.label: True generators
facts.value: Use a constantly changing physical attribute

facts.label: Pseudorandom numbers
facts.value: Reproducible from the initial state and method

facts.label: Ancient methods
facts.value: Dice, coin flipping, and shuffling playing cards

facts.label: Natural sources
facts.value: Atmospheric noise, thermal noise, radioactive decay

facts.label: Random number tables
facts.value: Collected results handed out because making numbers was slow

items.prompt: A programmer reruns a buggy simulation and wants exactly the same random numbers as before. What helps?

options.label: Switching to a hardware generator
Starting a pseudorandom generator from the same seed
Using a bigger sample
Letting the generator pick a new method

items.explain: A pseudorandom generator can run the same sequence again from the same random seed, which helps debugging.

items.prompt: Before computers, why were books of random number tables handed out to statisticians?

options.label: Dice and coins were banned in research
Statisticians could not read dice
Tables were more random than any physical method
Making large amounts of random numbers by hand took much work and time

items.explain: Mechanical methods needed much work and time for large quantities, so results were collected and distributed as tables.

items.prompt: A security product needs unpredictability above everything. Which kind of generator is generally preferred where feasible?

options.label: A hardware generator
A pseudorandom algorithm
A random number table
A coin flipped by the user

items.explain: Where unpredictability is paramount, such as in security applications, hardware generators are generally preferred over pseudorandom algorithms.

items.prompt: What does it mean that a pseudorandom number generator is predetermined?

options.label: Its numbers are written down in advance by hand
Its output is always a fixed single value
Anyone who knows its starting state and method can reproduce its numbers
It measures a physical source that never changes

items.explain: Pseudorandom numbers can be reproduced simply by knowing the initial state of the generator and the method it uses.

items.prompt: A music player is meant to feel random, yet it avoids playing the same song twice in a row. Why is that reasonable?

options.label: It need only seem random, and true randomness can repeat songs
True randomness would never repeat any single item
The generator has probably run out of entropy
Hardware generators are unable to handle music

items.explain: Such a system must only appear random; a truly random system would put no restriction on the same item appearing two or three times in succession.

items.prompt: A generator measures a natural source such as radioactive decay. Why might it be slow to deliver numbers?

options.label: Pseudorandom methods are always faster than natural ones
It can only collect entropy as fast as the physical phenomenon produces it
Natural sources must be reset daily
Radioactive decay needs a secret seed

items.explain: The speed of obtaining entropy depends on the physical phenomenon, so such sources are rate-limited until enough is harvested.
